# logflow-sim

> Open-source explainable log-pipeline simulator. Parses, validates,
> replays, diffs, and migrates log-routing configurations across 10
> dialects (rsyslog, syslog-ng, Fluent Bit, Vector, OpenTelemetry
> Collector, NXLog, Logstash, Filebeat, Promtail, Fluentd) with built-in
> Sigma detection-coverage analysis.

Live demo: https://netverdict.io/logflow/
Broken-config validator showcase: https://netverdict.io/logflow-broken/
Source code: https://github.com/gweber/logflow-sim
License: MIT
Maintainer: netverdict.io

## What problem this solves

Log-routing configs (rsyslog.conf, vector.toml, otel-collector.yaml, …)
are notoriously hard to reason about. Operators discover routing
regressions hours after merge when their SIEM goes quiet on a critical
source. logflow-sim turns the config into a normalized intermediate
representation and answers four operational questions:

1. **What does my config do?** — `simulate` shows the step-by-step
   trace for a single message: input selected, ruleset entered,
   conditions evaluated, lookups performed, variables changed, actions
   fired — each with the source file:line that produced the decision.
2. **What happens to my real traffic?** — `replay` runs a batch of
   syslog (text or pcap) through the config and reports aggregates:
   per-ruleset volume, per-output-target volume, top programs,
   silent-drop samples.
3. **What changes if I merge this PR?** — `diff` replays the same batch
   through baseline + overlay variants and reports per-output and
   per-ruleset deltas plus side-by-side per-message route changes.
4. **Will my detection rules still fire?** — `detection-impact` runs
   Sigma rules against the replay corpus; `detection/diff` shows
   per-rule firing deltas (the SOC-coverage equivalent of routing
   diff).

## Key documentation

- /docs/getting-started — install + first run
- /docs/api — REST API reference (every endpoint, JSON shapes,
  error format `{ error: { code, message, context } }`)
- /docs/supported-syntax — which rsyslog constructs are supported
- /docs/limitations — known gaps (queue semantics not simulated, no
  real file/network IO, no TLS-in-pcap)

## CLI surface

- `logflow-sim parse <conf-dir>` — parse + validator findings
- `logflow-sim test <conf-dir>` — parse + run conf/tests/*.json
- `logflow-sim simulate <conf-dir> --input=msg.json` — one message
- `logflow-sim replay <conf-dir> (--lines=FILE | --pcap=FILE)` — batch
- `logflow-sim diff <conf-dir> --overlay-dir=DIR --lines=FILE --max-route-change-pct=N`
- `logflow-sim convert <conf-dir> --target=DIALECT --out-dir=PATH`
- `logflow-sim detection-impact <conf-dir> --sigma=RULE.yml --lines=corpus.log`
- `logflow-sim detection-diff <conf-dir> --sigma=RULE.yml --overlay-dir=DIR --lines=corpus.log`

Exit codes: 0 success · 1 diagnostic / threshold breach · 2 test
failures · 3 bad invocation. `--format=github` emits
GitHub-Actions-annotation lines.

## GitHub Action

`gweber/logflow-sim@v1` — wraps the CLI for CI. The `command: diff`
flavor posts a sticky PR comment with the routing-impact verdict and
exits non-zero if `--max-route-change-pct` is breached.

## REST API surface (mounted at /api on the running server)

- POST /api/simulate — body `{ transport, port, programname, msg, ... }`
- POST /api/replay/lines — body `{ text | lines | ndjson, maxMessages? }`
- POST /api/replay/pcap — body `{ pcapBase64, maxMessages? }`
- POST /api/replay/diff — body `{ overlay: {path: content}, text | pcapBase64 }`
- POST /api/convert — body `{ target: "<dialect>" }` → multi-file output
- POST /api/detection/impact — body `{ sigmaText | sigma, text | pcapBase64 }`
- POST /api/detection/diff — body `{ sigmaText, overlay, text | pcapBase64 }`
- GET  /api/config/parse — model summary + parse + validator findings
- GET  /api/config/tree — file listing
- GET  /api/config/file?path=... — raw file contents
- GET  /api/dialects — registered dialects + display names

## Contribution surface

Validation rules (~50 LOC each), dialects (~200 LOC each), and i18n
translations (one JSON file each) are the contribution levers most
in demand. See CONTRIBUTING.md and .github/GOOD_FIRST_ISSUES.md in the
repo.
